outcomes: Decides in unlabeled queen-against-rook-and-pawn endings whether the weaker side holds or the stronger side breaks through
Names the one-step change that breaks a fortress
Holds a fortress against the engine for a set number of moves
sources: Items IE-FORT-* are generated by tools/endgames/gen_queen.py with tablebase claims; IBds77-10 and 18 to 20 are constructed and tablebase-checked

steps.text: The lesson *Fortresses: when more material cannot break through* gave three questions: covered entry squares, defenders that protect each other, and a safe waiting move. Now decide in positions with **no label**: can the weaker side hold, or does the stronger side break through? Predict win, draw or loss for the side to move, then check.

**Try the break before you rely on the fortress.** Name a move that wins a defender or forces the side to give way. If you cannot find one, the set-up may hold; if you can, test it. Rule of thumb: moving one defender can open a line for the queen, and a move that changes nothing important leaves the fortress standing. The tablebase decides.

steps.title: One step of one defender
steps.prompt: White is to move in all three. In the first the black pawn is on b7. In the second it has moved to b6. In the third the white king has moved from c3 to b3. Predict each result for White, then check.

steps.text: **Now hold one.** The next position is a draw if you keep the pieces protecting each other and find a safe waiting move. Play it against the engine: your goal is to hold. If a move loses a defender, press Stop when the game turns, then look at the position and name the break the engine used.

steps.prompt: Before each answer: did you look for the break first, or for the fortress first? What did the engine or the tablebase show that you had not looked for?

fields.label: What I had not looked for:

steps.text: **Remember.** To judge a possible fortress, first try the break: find a move that wins a defender or forces the side to give way. If you find none, the set-up may hold, so check that the defenders protect each other and a safe waiting move exists. If you do find one, test it. The tablebase has the last word.
